units.spine: The market squares are open to whoever brings custom in off the roads.
A garrison and a professional watch are kept here, both of them paid out of the town's purse.
People here can afford to argue about something other than money.
This town pays its own way well enough that the trades take apprentices on for the full term.
The citadel and the gates are kept sound, and nothing on either is for show.
The garrison can man the wall in strength, and the men it sends up have been up before.
Children here learn the rules about the dark early, and the rules hold.
The watch answers what is brought in at the door but goes looking for nothing in the streets.
Prices in the markets hold from one day to the next, and no trade here lives on its last sale.
The mages' guild can do what is usually wanted here, and it names what is beyond its people.
A living is made here out of standing on the way to somewhere else.
The town does not feed itself from its own ground, and what makes up the difference comes in on the road.
Rundgate has quarters that do not know one another, and a man out of the furrier's district is a stranger in the sage's quarter.
Nothing that has come at this town has changed the way it deals with its neighbours.
